Independent enumeration: base-five profiles, all first/second outcomes with integer weights in quarter-units, both final recipients tested by direct removal inequalities; positive upper witnesses (2,2,1) and (2,2,4)
correctness.rationale: For one singleton and one pair, the singleton owner's good must be weakly maximal in her values, with no further restriction. Fixing arrival-order tie breaks gives strict rankings for the proof without changing that sufficiency. When the first two rankings disagree, one first-coin outcome leaves both agents with their preferred early good; this succeeds unless both rank the third good top, in which case the other outcome, stacking the two early goods, succeeds. If both favor the first good, the success lower bound conditional on first recipient i is (1−T_i+T_j)/2 for T_i the indicator that the third ranks top; averaging cancels the indicators. If both favor the second, exactly one second-coin branch certifies success based on the other agent's top. For identical positive inputs (1,1,ε) and (1,1,L), 0<ε<1<L, only 1+2 splits can be EFX, and the first two goods must be split on the low-tail input and stacked on the high-tail input. The distribution on that decision is shared, so one success probability is at most 1/2. An independent direct enumeration of the policy found 9,200, 2,800, 3,625 profiles at probabilities 1/2, 3/4, 1 over {0,…,4}⁶, and checked all eight recipient strings for each of two positive tails.
residual_risks: Minor wording issue: ‘otherwise choose either recipient’ does not literally guarantee a 1+2 split; stacking the third on a no-completion branch gives 3+0. One may always choose a 1+2 split on such branches (and when 3+0 satisfies EFX, the empty agent values each good at zero and can instead receive the third). This does not affect the theorem. Enumeration is not a proof for all real values.
